subject: Snapshot quarantine & DPA addendum — backup purge timeline
messages:
From: Emma Riley <emma.riley@remedycare.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: Snapshot quarantine proposal and DPA addendum request

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, RemedyCare needs a short-term quarantine for nightly snapshots while we complete an internal compliance review and sign the DPA addendum. A few things we need clarified before proceeding:

- Proposed quarantine window for backups (how long will snapshots be held before purge?)
- Exact deletion workflow and what evidence (logs, manifests) Redwood can provide post-purge
- Any exceptions for KV/cache logs vs. full snapshot images (we may need certain logs to remain for forensic purposes)

Can you send a proposed schedule and a draft DPA addendum we can review with Legal? We need this to be scoped for EU data subjects — the compliance team will expect clear purge triggers and attestations.

Low urgency but target this week if possible.

Thanks,
Emma Riley
Head of Compliance — RemedyCare
AuditOps Team

Attachments: none
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Emma Riley <emma.riley@remedycare.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Snapshot quarantine proposal and DPA addendum request

Emma —

Appreciate the clear list. Attached is a first-pass schedule (remedy_backup_quarantine_proposal_v1.xlsx) and a DPA addendum template scoped for the EU (DPA_Addendum_RemedyCare.docx). High level summary of our proposal: 

- Snapshot quarantine window: temporary hold of 120 calendar days from snapshot creation unless a shorter window is requested in writing.
- Purge triggers: automated purge job runs daily; retention TTL applied per-snapshot. Purge is queued, deleted objects are recorded in a deletion manifest with timestamp and operator id.
- Evidence: we will provide a CSV manifest, S3 object versions (where applicable), and an audit log extract showing deletion events.
- Log carveouts: we differentiate between KV/cache telemetry and persistent snapshot images. By default KV/cache logs are on a 30-day TTL; persistent images follow the quarantine window above.

Questions for you:
1) Is RemedyCare comfortable with a 120-day quarantine for the snapshots, or do you want a shorter maximum (90 days would be fine for us if that helps expedite approval)?
2) Do you require an irrevocable deletion certificate or will the deletion manifest + audit extract suffice?

Kimberly/Marissa/Irene — can you review and confirm operational feasibility (esp. the manifest format and the evidence export cadence)? I noted EU region to ensure we route to the correct jurisdictional backup store.

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments: remedy_backup_quarantine_proposal_v1.xlsx; DPA_Addendum_RemedyCare.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Emma Riley <emma.riley@remedycare.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 13:30:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Snapshot quarantine proposal and DPA addendum request

Thanks for the writeup and attachments. A few operational notes from the backup/infra side: 

- 120 days is feasible, but for EU-regulated datasets I recommend splitting: 90 days for persistent images + a separate 180-day forensic buffer for encrypted KV logs that contain audit trails. We can implement the forensic buffer as an encrypted escrow bucket with strict access control (ops-only) and separate deletion process.
- Deletion manifest: our standard is a newline-delimited JSON( ndjson ) with fields: snapshot_id, object_key, deleted_at, operator, deletion_proof_link. We can also provide CSV on request.
- Evidence cadence: we can run an evidence export job daily and drop a signed digest to the shared drive location you provided. The daily digest will contain checksums and a GPG-signed timestamp.

A couple of clarifying asks:
- Emma: if you prefer a single uniform TTL (e.g., 90 days) instead of the split above, call it out — it changes the escrow/ops steps.
- Legal: do you require DocuSign for the addendum, or is an emailed signed PDF acceptable?

Quoted for context:
> Mateo Alvarez wrote:
> > - Snapshot quarantine window: temporary hold of 120 calendar days from snapshot creation unless a shorter window is requested in writing.
> > - Purge triggers: automated purge job runs daily; retention TTL applied per-snapshot. Purge is queued, deleted objects are recorded in a deletion manifest with timestamp and operator id.

I'll standby and finalize the manifest/export examples once we lock the TTL.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Backup & Data Ops — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Snapshot quarantine proposal and DPA addendum request

Team —

Thanks, this is helpful. RemedyCare legal would prefer a maximum uniform TTL of 90 days for snapshots (we can accept a separate escrowed forensic buffer for KV logs at 180 days if you implement strict access controls and provide deletion attestations). Two quick asks to move to signature:

1) Please update the DPA addendum to reflect: 90-day snapshot TTL for EU data + 180-day encrypted escrow for KV logs (ops-only access).
2) Provide the DocuSign packet for the addendum and a sample deletion manifest from a test purge run (even a simulated one) so our auditors can validate fields.

If you can send the updated addendum via DocuSign and drop a simulated manifest to the Drive link, Legal will fast-track.

Agreeing to the timeline: target to have DocuSign sent by EOD Monday so we can review and sign mid-week.

Best,
Emma Riley
Head of Compliance — RemedyCare
AuditOps Team
